newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL SHARES END LOWER FOR THIRD STRAIGHT SESSION.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL SHARES END LOWER FOR THIRD STRAIGHT SESSION.

text.p: Brazilian stocks seesawed on Tuesday before closing lower for a third consecutive session, as a slump on Wall Street and speculation ahead of Wednesday's futures index expiration weighed on the market, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 47 most traded shares closed off 1.16 percent at 11,810 points.
Total market turnover was lighter-than-average at 656.01 million reais ($607.4 million).
Amid an absence of fresh domestic news, the bolsa again mirrored U.S. stocks, which showed sharp declines.

Traders expect the next session to be pretty much the same, with the focus fixed squarely on Wall Street. Key U.S. economic reports, which may indicate a trend for interest rates, are due out on Wednesday.
Analysts said Tuesday's Senate approval of the nomination of Gustavo Franco as central bank president was widely expected and had little impact on stock prices.
Among leading Brazilian stocks, benchmark Telebras preferred closed off 2.18 percent at 143.80 reais.
State oil company Petrobras preferred rose 0.33 percent to close at 304 reais.
Federal power holding company Eletrobras preferred fell 0.34 percent, ending at 580 reais.
Preferred shares of CVRD, the recently privatized mining company, preferred rose 0.76 percent to end at 27.91 reais.
The Sao Paulo bolsa's power sector index .IEE fell a slight 0.05 percent to 3,412 points.
